about: One router per push (scripts/ci/pr_router.py, .github/workflows/pr-router.yml, RFD 0023). Each callee: the pull_request activity types and path filter that used to start it on its own, and optionally `affects`, the inputs it reads. Edit this file and pr-router.yml together; `python3 scripts/ci/pr_router.py check` says whether they agree.

cmux-machine-channel.yml.affects_why: PR_HEAD_FAST_LANE (cmux-machine-channel.yml): a full-tier head (the land tier, once land-judge adds ready-to-land or full-ci; never a cheap or draft head) gets the Cloud machine channel's thin Linux pair built before merge, so the merge points the channel without its own cargo build. Its plan job builds only when the head's merge with the base changes the v2 tree key (scripts/cmux-next/cmux-tui-tree-inputs.txt, over a dozen roots and growing, so the key decides, not a path list), and only for this repository's heads.
cmux-machine-channel.yml.land_handoff_only_why: Built only on the land's own heads: the labeled event that adds ready-to-land or full-ci, or land's update-branch head of a ready-to-land PR. Both labels stay on a PR across later pushes (759 of 3,722 open PRs carried ready-to-land on 11-25), so gating on the full tier built about 168 PR heads an hour against about 17 merges (2026-11-26 04:47-06:05Z: 228 x86_64 + 221 aarch64 builds, 217 branches, 22 merges, about 2.5k machine-h/day).

cmux-next-size-budget.yml.affects_why: bundle-size-pr.py check measures three inputs (scripts/cmux-next/bundle-size-budget.json pull_request): files under tree_paths (Resources, Packages/macOS/*/Sources/*/Resources, Assets.xcassets), the web bundles (inputs: web-bundle-key.py --routed, a superset here by directory), and the crates of shipped Rust binaries (Cargo manifests and lockfiles); plus the tool itself under scripts/cmux-next. A change touching none of them adds nothing to the app.

classic-api-guard.yml.affects_why: classic_api_guard.py warns into feat-cmux-next only when a changed path is under a guarded deploy of scripts/ci/classic-auto-deploy.json (every guarded path, 2026-11-21, is under web/, config/iroh/ or workers/presence/; by directory here so a path added there stays covered); otherwise it prints a notice and passes. The guard and its list run from the base, so their own change is listed only to exercise the workflow. A routed edit (the `Classic API change:` line, the base) reaches it through pr-router.yml's route `if:`. Last 300 merges: the old trigger started it on 300, this on 14.

swift-linux-packages.yml.affects_why: Every package it tests (scripts/ci/swift-linux-packages.txt and the matrix's shared, mobile-core and stack-auth groups) lives under Packages/Shared, Packages/iOS or vendor/stack-auth-swift-sdk-prerelease, and their local path dependencies stay inside Packages/Shared (none reaches Packages/macOS, 2026-11-21), except CmuxNext's Linux shape: the targets of linuxTargetNames and their tests, and CCmuxAppFFI, which it links as libcmux_app_ffi.a built from the cmux-tui crates by scripts/ci/app_ffi_linux.py over build-app-ffi.sh's headers (2026-11-26); package-test-lane.sh sources swift-test-debug-info.sh and swiftpm-binary-module-guard.sh. The ios-kit group tests cmux-next-ios/CmuxMobileKit (its only path dependency outside the kit is Packages/Shared/CMUXAuthCore). Last 300 merges: the old filter started it on 96, this on 9. The ios-kit group also reads the connection contract fixture (rust/crates/cmux-mobile-link-ffi/tests/fixtures/connection_contract.json, cmux-next-ios/contract/README.md): a Rust change to it must run the Swift side. Every file outside the kit its listed test targets read (the Rust fixtures, schemas/deeplinks, schemas/notice-timing, design/icons/source, verify/agent-cli-hybrid) is in EXTRA_INPUTS of scripts/ci/swift_linux_reach.py, which routes it to the ios-kit group and the kit's listed row; before 11-27 the planner sent the fixture to no group, so the Swift side never ran on a Rust-only change (tests/test_swift_linux_reach.py finds every such read).

pr-pipeline.yml.table_why: The step table's jobs this workflow runs (ci/steps.toml, `ci/run`). It starts when the change routes a step of one of them: a step's `inputs` are the path filter of the workflow it replaced. It starts on a full-tier head only (pr_router.py FULL_TIER_JOBS lists all four jobs): a cheap head, a draft or a ready head before `ready-to-land` or `full-ci` (head_tier.py), starts none of linux, web-browser, ios or mac; adding either label, or marking the draft ready, runs it on the same head before any merge. Until 11-25 it ran on drafts and cheap heads (`draft` let it), costing about 50k runner-minutes a day (Leo, 2026-11-21: "de facto, im asking for 99% fewer minutes of ci time, period."). `draft` stays so a fast-track head (full tier, docs or tests only) still runs the steps it routes. Each job runs only when the change routes a step of it (the router's `table` output, pr-pipeline.yml's job `if:`s). The `mac` and `ios` jobs are not routed on a pull request since 2026-11-26: in 641 sampled merges over 30 days no Mac compile or Swift/iOS test job had a real catch (a red a later code change on the pull request turned green), and the two legs held 22.8k Mac minutes in the 10 hours to 2026-11-25T23Z, 85% of their jobs red (cmuxterm-hq docs/findings/2026-11-25-ci-value.md). After merge: cmux-next.yml's fast tier on the push, and the post-merge batch (bisect and revert): suite fast-tier for the cargo and script entries, suites pr-pipeline-mac and pr-pipeline-ios for every mac and ios step the window's paths route (`ci/run`, as here).

screen-share-drop-gate.yml.affects_why: The gate builds cmux-rd from cmux-rd-host (its own Cargo workspace, which pulls the link, proto and transport crates by path) and runs scripts/screen-share-netem.py from cmux-rd-host's tree; nothing else changes what it measures.

ios-link-ffi-linux.yml.affects_why: The cross-commit component test pairs this PR's iPhone link with the last three published Mac hosts, and the last three processed TestFlight iPhone links with this PR's host, over WebRTC and WireGuard plus daemon identify. The fast-gates required status waits for it even with a local test receipt. Swift pairing and terminal projection changes also select this transport prerequisite; this Linux test does not execute the Swift app or prove its UI. The local Cargo dependency closure, inherited workspace manifests, toolchains and Cargo configuration also route this gate; the closure regression detects new shared transport or projection dependencies.
ios-link-ffi-linux.yml.draft_why: Pairing and transport regressions must be caught at every affected head, including drafts.

cmux-next-compile-preflight.yml.affects_why: The preflight reads web-bundle-key.py --routed: all webviews, its checked-in protocol IR, design and type schemas, release highlights, Resources and macOS catalogs, the web bundle builders and Bun pin, plus the external files imported by shipped webviews (examples, cloud generated types, vite-plus checks and the model catalog). These directory supersets fail open for newly added imports, while docs, Rust sources outside the protocol IR and unrelated tooling do not start the Linux runner. Unknown changed files still start it because pr_router.py routes more when it cannot read the diff.
cmux-next-compile-preflight.yml.draft_why: A web-affecting draft still gets the fast build safety check; an unaffected draft has no compile-preflight caller job.

cmux-next-fast-gates.yml.affects_why: No path filter (it had none as its own pull_request trigger): every head the router starts anything for starts it, and its jobs' own `if:`s keep their tier rules (a draft, a cheap or a not-yet-landing head skips resolve as before), so `draft` only lets those `if:`s decide. A head the router starts nothing for (head_tier's `none`: an idle or green-head base merge) starts none of its jobs; until 11-26 each such head still started its jobs (cmux-next-fast-gates.yml 32k runner-minutes in the 24 h to 2026-11-26; Leo, 2026-11-21: "de facto, im asking for 99% fewer minutes of ci time, period."). `labeled` is listed as its trigger had it; the router turns an added ready-to-land or full-ci into ready_for_review and skips any other label.

swift-acpmux-protocol.yml.affects_why: swift-logic-delta.py --gate counts swift_logic_lines + mirror_lines (swift-logic-lines.py) at the base and the merge commit: it reads only Swift files, the class table plans/cmux-next/swift-logic-classes.tsv and its own counter. A change touching none of them moves neither number. Before: the 400 feat-cmux-next merges to 2026-11-25T23Z added 3,334 lines in 43 PRs, none asked why.

nightly-pr-build.yml.land_ask_only_why: On the affected landing tier it starts only when land asks: the labeled event adding ready-to-land or full-ci (land-judge pulses it at the head it lands) and the merge train's tip, not on each push or base merge of a labelled or ask-named PR. 15-21Z 2026-11-27 its two Mac stubs were the 2nd and 3rd largest jobs (arm64 17.9, x86_64 17.5 runner-min per merged PR, 11,896 runner-min): 80% on PRs not merged by 21Z, 56% on base-merge heads, 25% on pushes after the label, and 31% of runs repeated an input key already compiled. $CI_NIGHTLY_PR_BUILD_AT_LAND=0 starts it on every landing head again.
nightly-pr-build.yml.affects_why: The Nightly's app compile reads the packages, vendored sources, resources, the Xcode project and the compile script with what it sources; the helpers read cmux-tui, cmux-next-ios/rust, Native/OptChat and DiffSidecar and the cargo config. nightly_pr_build.py route narrows it per build; nothing else changes what it builds.

transcript-replay-perf-report.yml.affects_why: webviews/bench/transcript-replay-ab.sh replays the long chat into the agent pane built from webviews/src/agent-session (and what it imports) at the merge base and the head, with the head's bench and its imports (browsers, godFixture, perfRow, replayLogs, stability, support/sharedBuilds, test/support foldFrameReport and paintedFrames); the duress reading runs scripts/measure/replay-under-load.sh and its bench; the summary is scripts/ci/transcript_replay_report.py. A change touching none of them moves no number in the report.
